GET /rest/api/3/myself
  Says whose token the app holds. Sign-in calls it to check the credentials before it stores anything, and every launch calls it again; a 401 means the token was refused or stopped working.
  auth: HTTP Basic with an email and an API token
    not compared at 200 displayName: the environment names its accounts, and the book knows the standing account only by its account id
    not compared at 200 accountType: atlassian for a person, app for a bot
    not compared at 200 emailAddress: privacy settings may hide it
    not compared at 200 timeZone: the environment names its accounts, and the book knows the standing account only by its account id
    not compared at 200 avatarUrls: a URL on the site the book plays against
    not compared at 200 self: a URL on the site the book plays against
  200 → User: the account the email and token belong to
  401 → bytes: the email and token are missing, or Jira no longer accepts the token
    why: Jira answers before it reads the request, with a line of text and no error collection
  carries: ReadMyself
source: https://dac-static.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/swagger-v3.v3.json::GET /rest/api/3/myself
source: https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/basic-auth-for-rest-apis/

  auth: HTTP Basic with an email and an API token
  query:
    startAt     integer — 0, then the next page's start
    maxResults  integer — at most 100; 50 when left out
    orderBy     string — name; key when left out
    not compared at 200 values[].id: the site numbers it, and two sites number the same record apart
    not compared at 200 values[].self: a URL on the site the book plays against
    not compared at 200 values[].avatarUrls: a URL on the site the book plays against
    not compared at 200 total: it counts or pages everything the site holds, which other people's records swell
    not compared at 200 isLast: it counts or pages everything the site holds, which other people's records swell
    not compared at 200 self: a URL on the site the book plays against
    not compared at 200 nextPage: a URL on the site the book plays against
  200 → PageOfProjects: one page of the projects the caller may browse, by name
  401 → bytes: the email and token are missing, or Jira no longer accepts the token
    why: Jira answers before it reads the request, with a line of text and no error collection
  carries: ListProjects
source: https://dac-static.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/swagger-v3.v3.json::GET /rest/api/3/project/search

    startAt     integer
    maxResults  integer — 1000 for the session's first read, 50 while the person types; 1000 when left out
    not compared at 200 startAt: it counts or pages everything the site holds, which other people's records swell
    not compared at 200 total: it counts or pages everything the site holds, which other people's records swell
    not compared at 200 isLast: it counts or pages everything the site holds, which other people's records swell

  401 → bytes: the email and token are missing, or Jira no longer accepts the token
    why: Jira answers before it reads the request, with a line of text and no error collection
  carries: ListLabels

GET /rest/api/3/user/assignable/search
  Offers the people the Assignee picker may choose: only those who may be assigned the issue.
  auth: HTTP Basic with an email and an API token
  query:
    query       string classes: the standing account's name ('manager') — text the person types; everyone assignable when left out
    maxResults  integer — 50
    issueKey    id of IssueRecord (string) — the issue being assigned, in the detail pane
    project     string — the project of a new issue, in the create dialog
    not compared at 200 [].displayName: the environment names its accounts, and the book knows the standing account only by its account id
    not compared at 200 [].accountType: atlassian for a person, app for a bot
    not compared at 200 [].emailAddress: privacy settings may hide it
    not compared at 200 [].timeZone: the environment names its accounts, and the book knows the standing account only by its account id
    not compared at 200 [].avatarUrls: a URL on the site the book plays against
    not compared at 200 [].self: a URL on the site the book plays against
  200 → [User] (any order: Jira returns people in no documented order): the people who hold Assign issues on the issue or project and match the query; a page may hold fewer than asked
  404 → ErrorCollection: no issue has that key, or the caller may not browse it
  401 → bytes: the email and token are missing, or Jira no longer accepts the token
    why: Jira answers before it reads the request, with a line of text and no error collection
  carries: FindAssignable
    refuses 404 'Issue does not exist or you do not have permission to see it.'
source: https://dac-static.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/swagger-v3.v3.json::GET /rest/api/3/user/assignable/search

GET /rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}/statuses
  Gives each issue type's statuses with their categories. The Issues view groups by category and the status filter lists these names.
  auth: HTTP Basic with an email and an API token
  path:
    projectIdOrKey  string (required) — the project key, such as CASE
    not compared at 200 [].statuses[].id: company-managed projects share status ids, so the book knows a status by its project and name
    not compared at 200 [].statuses[].statusCategory.id: Jira numbers the categories, and only the key is what the app reads
    not compared at 200 [].statuses[].statusCategory.name: the category's display name follows the site's language
    not compared at 200 [].statuses[].statusCategory.colorName: a colour the app does not draw
    not compared at 200 [].statuses[].statusCategory.self: a URL on the site the book plays against
    not compared at 200 [].statuses[].self: a URL on the site the book plays against
    not compared at 200 [].statuses[].description: text an admin writes
    not compared at 200 [].statuses[].iconUrl: a URL on the site the book plays against
    not compared at 200 [].id: company-managed projects share issue type ids
    not compared at 200 [].self: a URL on the site the book plays against
  200 → [IssueTypeWithStatus] (any order: Jira documents no order for a project's issue types): one entry per issue type, each with the statuses its workflow holds and their categories
  404 → ErrorCollection: no project has that key, or the caller may not browse it
  401 → bytes: the email and token are missing, or Jira no longer accepts the token
    why: Jira answers before it reads the request, with a line of text and no error collection
  carries: ReadProjectStatuses
    refuses 404 "No project could be found with key '{projectIdOrKey}'."

GET /rest/api/3/issue/createmeta/{projectIdOrKey}/issuetypes
  Lists the types the person may create. Level 0 types fill the type filter and the create dialog, and level 1 types are the epic types. The deprecated createmeta with expand is never called.
  auth: HTTP Basic with an email and an API token
  path:
    projectIdOrKey  string (required) — the project key, such as CASE
    not compared at 200 issueTypes[].id: company-managed projects share issue type ids
    not compared at 200 issueTypes[].description: text an admin writes
    not compared at 200 issueTypes[].iconUrl: a URL on the site the book plays against
    not compared at 200 issueTypes[].self: a URL on the site the book plays against
    not compared at 200 total: a site may offer a sub-task type the mockup world leaves out
  200 → PageOfCreateMetaIssueTypes: the types the caller may create in the project, with their hierarchy level
  404 → ErrorCollection: no project has that key, or the caller may not browse it
  401 → bytes: the email and token are missing, or Jira no longer accepts the token
    why: Jira answers before it reads the request, with a line of text and no error collection
  carries: ListCreatableTypes
    refuses 404 "No project could be found with key '{projectIdOrKey}'."
source: https://dac-static.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/swagger-v3.v3.json::GET /rest/api/3/issue/createmeta/{projectIdOrKey}/issuetypes
source: https://community.developer.atlassian.com/t/create-issue-meta-endpoint-deprecation/75413

GET /rest/api/3/issue/createmeta/{projectIdOrKey}/issuetypes/{issueTypeId}
  Gives the create screen of one type, field by field. The create dialog lists exactly these fields in this order and marks the required ones; the app pages until total.
  auth: HTTP Basic with an email and an API token
  path:
    projectIdOrKey  string (required) — the project key
    issueTypeId     id of IssueTypeRecord (string) (required) — the site's id of the issue type
  query:
    startAt     integer — 0 when left out
    maxResults  integer — 200, the largest page; 50 when left out
    not compared at 200 fields[].schema.customId: the site numbers it, and two sites number the same record apart
    not compared at 200 fields[].schema.configuration: the type's settings, which the app does not read
    not compared at 200 fields[].key: the field's key, which repeats its id
    not compared at 200 fields[].allowedValues: option objects whose ids the site numbers; the edit tests pick by value
    not compared at 200 fields[].hasDefaultValue: an admin sets defaults per context
    not compared at 200 fields[].defaultValue: an admin sets defaults per context
    not compared at 200 fields[].autoCompleteUrl: a URL on the site the book plays against
    not compared at 200 fields[].configuration: the field's settings, which the app does not read
    not compared at 200 total: a site's create screen may hold system fields, such as Reporter or Attachment, the mockup world leaves out
    not compared at 200 results: the schema lists it beside fields; the app reads fields
  200 → PageOfCreateMetaIssueTypeWithField: the create screen's fields in the screen's order, each with required, its schema and its operations
  400 → ErrorCollection: maxResults is over 200
  404 → ErrorCollection: no project has that key, or the caller may not browse it
  401 → bytes: the email and token are missing, or Jira no longer accepts the token
    why: Jira answers before it reads the request, with a line of text and no error collection
  carries: ReadCreateFields
    refuses 400 "Parameter 'maxResults' must not exceed the limit '200'"
      why: createmeta pages its fields by at most 200, so the app asks for 200 and pages until total
    refuses 404 "No project could be found with key '{projectIdOrKey}'."
source: https://dac-static.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/swagger-v3.v3.json::GET /rest/api/3/issue/createmeta/{projectIdOrKey}/issuetypes/{issueTypeId}
source: https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-issues/

  auth: HTTP Basic with an email and an API token
  path:
    boardId  id of BoardRecord (integer) (required) — the board's id
    not compared at 200 filter.self: a URL on the site the book plays against
    not compared at 200 columnConfig.columns[].statuses[].id: company-managed projects share status ids
    not compared at 200 columnConfig.columns[].statuses[].self: a URL on the site the book plays against
    not compared at 200 columnConfig.columns[].min: WIP limits are out of the app's scope
    not compared at 200 columnConfig.columns[].max: WIP limits are out of the app's scope
    not compared at 200 columnConfig.constraintType: WIP limits are out of the app's scope
    not compared at 200 self: a URL on the site the book plays against
    not compared at 200 location: the project the board sits in
    not compared at 200 estimation: the estimation field the board names, which the seed leaves as the template sets it

  404 → ErrorCollection: no board has that id, or the caller may not see it

    refuses 404 'Board does not exist or you do not have permission to see it.'
source: https://dac-static.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/software/swagger.v3.json::GET /rest/agile/1.0/board/{boardId}/configuration

GET /rest/agile/1.0/board/{boardId}/sprint
  Gives a scrum board's active and future sprints. They fill the board header, the sprint sections and every sprint picker.
  auth: HTTP Basic with an email and an API token
  path:
    boardId  id of BoardRecord (integer) (required) — the board's id
  query:
    state  string — active,future; every state when left out
    not compared at 200 values[].startDate: the seed sets a sprint's dates on the day it runs
    not compared at 200 values[].endDate: the seed sets a sprint's dates on the day it runs
    not compared at 200 values[].createdDate: the site's clock stamps it
    not compared at 200 values[].self: a URL on the site the book plays against
    not compared at 200 isLast: it counts or pages everything the site holds, which other people's records swell
  200 → PageOfSprints: the board's active and future sprints with their names, goals and dates
  400 → ErrorCollection: the board is a kanban board, which has no sprints
  404 → ErrorCollection: no board has that id, or the caller may not see it
  401 → bytes: the email and token are missing, or Jira no longer accepts the token
    why: Jira answers before it reads the request, with a line of text and no error collection
  carries: ListBoardSprints
    refuses 404 'Board does not exist or you do not have permission to see it.'
    refuses 400 'The board does not support sprints'
      why: only a scrum board has sprints; a kanban board's issues come from its board and backlog lists
source: https://dac-static.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/software/swagger.v3.json::GET /rest/agile/1.0/board/{boardId}/sprint

GET /rest/api/3/filter/{filterId}
  Gives a board filter's JQL. It is the kanban backlog's fallback: if the backlog list refuses a kanban board, the app searches the filter's JQL narrowed to the backlog column's statuses.
  auth: HTTP Basic with an email and an API token
  path:
    filterId  id of FilterRecord (string) (required) — the board filter's id, from the board configuration
    not compared at 200 name: the board template names the filter
    not compared at 200 self: a URL on the site the book plays against
    not compared at 200 owner: the environment names its accounts, and the book knows the standing account only by its account id
    not compared at 200 viewUrl: a URL on the site the book plays against
    not compared at 200 searchUrl: a URL on the site the book plays against
    not compared at 200 favourite: a person's choice
  200 → Filter: the filter's JQL
  400 → ErrorCollection: the filter does not exist or the caller may not see it
  401 → bytes: the email and token are missing, or Jira no longer accepts the token
    why: Jira answers before it reads the request, with a line of text and no error collection
  carries: ReadFilter
    refuses 400 'The selected filter is not available to you, perhaps it has been deleted or had its permissions changed.'
source: https://dac-static.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/swagger-v3.v3.json::GET /rest/api/3/filter/{id}
source: https://community.atlassian.com/forums/Jira-questions/Accessing-Backlog-Issues-on-Kanban-Boards-via-JIRA-REST-API/qaq-p/2697457

ManageIssuesInAProject
A manager opens CASE. The app reads the project's statuses and the types they may create, then lists the open Bugs, Stories and
    Tasks. They create a Bug: the dialog reads the Bug create screen, and Create without Severity is refused with the error under Severity,
    so they fill it and the Bug is created. They create a Story, open it, retitle it, describe it, raise its priority, assign it to
    themselves from the assignable people, set its Reviewer from the site's people and add a label, reading each change back. The status
    picker offers the workflow's transitions; they start the Story, send it to review and cannot send it back to To Do, because CASE's
    workflow has no such transition. They finish it, and it leaves the open list for the done list. A field the Story's screen lacks is
    refused with Jira's message under the field.

ManageEpicsInAProject
A manager opens Epics in CASE1, a team-managed project, where epics work the same way as in a company-managed one. The app reads the
    types to tell epics from standard types and lists the open epics. They create an epic, which has no children yet. They create a child
    story inside it, then add an existing task through Add existing, which sets the task's parent. The progress search counts both
    children by status; when the story is done, one of two is done. They remove the task from the epic, which clears its parent, and it
    shows on the Issues view with no epic chip. Finishing the epic moves it out of the open epics and into the list of every epic.

The sandbox holds the seeded issues and every earlier run's issues, so a run finds what it made by its label and never counts a list other people write to. This is the live tests' own rule: they label the issues they make with `j4m-live` and the run's id.

A label exists once an issue carries it. Jira has no call that creates one, so the label list grows by the creates and edits that send a new string. The app keeps no list of statuses, boards, sprints, field names or people. It reads each project's statuses with their categories, its boards, each board's active and future sprints, and an issue's fields with their names, schemas and edit metadata in one read of `fields=*all&expand=names,schema,editmeta`. The book reads the same calls and compares what the seeded world fixes: status names and categories, board names and types, sprint names, states and goals, and the values of the fields a journey set.

People are known by account id. The Assignee picker reads only who may be assigned the issue or the project, and any other user field reads everyone on the site, so Jira can still refuse a person a field limits to some groups. The book knows one person, the standing account, and finds it by its name in both searches. Other people's rows drop out of the comparison, because the environment names its accounts.

The detail read's names, schemas and edit metadata are maps over every field of the site, which may hold fields the mockup world leaves out. The book leaves them to the site and checks the create screens field by field instead.

Jira answers a refused create or edit with `{"errorMessages": [...], "errors": {"<field id>": "<message>"}}`. A required custom field left empty comes back under its `customfield_<n>` id, as `Severity is required.` under Severity's id, and a field the screen lacks comes back as `Field '<id>' cannot be set. It is not on the appropriate screen, or unknown.`. The app shows each message under its field and the rest in the dialog.

A refusal the book compares is the first of `errorMessages`, else `<field id>: <message>` for the first field error, so the field a message belongs to is part of what the run checks. Custom field ids differ from site to site, so the book writes a custom field as `cf[<name>]` and the surface swaps the site's id in and out; see standing-records-are-named-by-name.md.
The book's create screens are the mockup world's: CASE requires Severity on a Bug and OPS requires Affected service, a cascading select the app cannot fill.

A status changes only through a transition the workflow offers from the issue's status, and the app reads the offer before it runs one. The seeded workflows let every status reach every other, except that CASE has no transition from In Review back to To Do. No workflow offers the status the issue already holds. A transition the issue does not offer is refused as `Transition id '<id>' is not valid for this issue.`; the surface names the id by the status it leads to, since two workflows of one site reuse the same ids.

The app never sends a transition screen's fields. When the chosen transition shows a screen with a required field and no default, the app does not run it and offers the browser. The book models that state as an admin putting a screen with a required Resolution on the transitions into Done, which refuses the call with `resolution: Resolution is required.`. Neither environment lets the book arrange that while it runs, so the cells that need it are skipped; QUESTIONS.md asks for the knob. A transition is never retried, because a repeat could move the issue twice.

GetMyself: which email and API token does `cargo xtask fake-jira` accept? Nothing written names the fake's credential, so the backstage sends `ana.ruiz@acme-labs.test` with `fake-jira-token` when `JIRA_EMAIL` and `JIRA_TOKEN` are unset.
GetMyself: what body does Jira Cloud give a 401 for a refused or missing Basic credential? The book expects the text `Client must be authenticated to access this resource.` with no error collection.

ScreenGoesOnDone: can the fake Jira put a screen on a transition while it runs? The test-environment note gives it only `--transition-screen` at start, and the sandbox needs an admin in the browser, so the book cannot arrange a transition that needs a screen.

RunTransition: what does Jira answer when a transition's screen requires a field the call leaves out? The research leaves it UNCONFIRMED, and the book expects 400 with `errors.resolution` set to `Resolution is required.`.
RunTransition: does Jira refuse a global transition into the status the issue already holds with `Transition id '<id>' is not valid for this issue.`?

MoveToSprint: what message does Jira give a move of more than 50 issues, and does it count the issues before it looks any up? The book names one issue 51 times and expects `Cannot move more than 50 issues at once.`.
MoveToSprint: what does Jira answer a sprint id that is not a number? The book expects 404 `Sprint does not exist or you do not have permission to see it.`.
SearchIssues: how does Jira order `ORDER BY status`? The book orders by the status's place in the project's workflow, then by rank.
SearchIssues: what does Jira answer a search with no JQL or a blank one? The book expects 400 `Unbounded JQL queries are not allowed here. Please add a search restriction to your query.`.
SearchIssues: what does Jira answer a page token no page gave? The book expects 400 `The provided next page token is invalid or expired.`.

CreateIssue: what does Jira answer a body whose field has the wrong JSON type, or a create with no fields? The book expects 400 `Invalid request payload. Refer to the REST API documentation and try again.` for every malformed body.
FindUsers: what does Jira answer a user search with no query? The book expects 400 `One of the following query parameters must be provided: query, accountId, property.`.
ListBoardSprints: what does Jira answer a sprint list on a kanban board? The book expects 400 `The board does not support sprints`.
ReadFilter: does Jira answer a filter that does not exist with 400 and `The selected filter is not available to you, perhaps it has been deleted or had its permissions changed.`?
